craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as non-duality; vyabhicāri wonder at the undivided individual (C1 rasa block). Sanskrit-first: na kiṃcid…dvaitam (NOTHING stands dual — total negation opens); svaprakāśāt…ekadhāmani (from self-luminosity, in the one abode — ground before consequence); na bhajyeta (would NEVER be divided — optative-passive kept as ‘would never’). Rows: 9 (no-split / never-divided echo — the denial returns as protection), 1 (‘divided’ end-weighted — what cannot happen closes the verse), 11 (deixis thinned: ‘this and that’ kept bare, no pointing). Close: ‘would never be divided’. Rupture: the em-dash after ‘that’ (all-things named, then the ground: consciousness). Rejected: ‘in two’ for ‘dually’ — killed: dvaita is the doctrine-word; splitting L1 at the semicolon — killed: semicolon already breathes, a triplet would strand ‘no split’. Read aloud: NO-thing at ALL stands DU-al-ly a-PART … IN-con-SCIOUS-ness there IS no SPLIT … would NE-ver be di-VID-ed.

lines: Nothing at all stands dually apart from knowledge; made of this and that, in consciousness there is no split.
From self-luminosity, a hundredfold, in the one abode — the individual would never be divided.
l4.sanskrit_cite: jñānadvibhinno na hi kaścidarthaḥ tattatkṛtaḥ saṃvidi nāsti bhedaḥ | svayamprakāśācchatam aikadhāmni prātisvikī nāpi vibheditā syāt

reads_against.argmap: No thing stands dually apart from knowledge; in consciousness there is no difference; the individual, in the one abode of self-luminosity, stays undivided. → Non-duality: nothing apart from knowledge.
